complexity.correctness_reason: lists = [[]] (an initially empty list, which NeetCode's Example 3 permits) is never deleted and never matched, so once the real chains are exhausted `i` is stale or unassigned and `prev.next = lists[i]` raises IndexError/UnboundLocalError.
complexity.notes: The added `if lists[j]:` guard doesn't actually fix empty chains: an initially empty list is never removed, and on a pass where every remaining entry is empty `i` keeps a stale index from a previous iteration, so `lists[i]` raises. There is a standard O(n log k) route via ||a min-heap over the chain heads, or pairwise divide-and-conquer merging||, which would drop the benchmark to n log n on this ladder. The `min_val` bookkeeping is redundant since `min(...)` is recomputed on the same comparison just done.
complexity.summary: For each output node, scans every remaining chain head to find the minimum value (short-circuiting on a head equal to the last emitted value), splices that node on, and deletes exhausted chains; this head-rescan makes it O(n*k) total.
